title: Stock detail page: help icon on every metric explaining what it is, its Elder methodology basis, and the current value
description:
User request: on the stock detail view, every displayed element should have a small question-mark icon in its top-right corner; clicking it opens an explanation of (1) what the metric/signal is, (2) how it relates to Dr. Elder's Triple Screen/Impulse/confidence-scoring methodology, and (3) where possible, an interpretation of the CURRENT value shown (not just a static definition) -- e.g. for a Stochastic %K of 36.9, something like 'in the neutral zone (30-70): neither overbought nor oversold'. Ground every explanation in docs/Analyse.md's actual definitions (§2 Triple Screen, §3 Impulse System, §4 Indicator Summary, §5 Signal Logic, §6 Confidence Score) -- do not invent methodology text not backed by that doc.

Cover every distinct metric currently shown on StockDetailPage: SignalSummary (the Signal itself, Confidence score, each of the 5 confidence-breakdown components), ScreensPanel (Tide trend + weekly MACD-H slope, Impulse color, Wave's Stochastic %K + Force Index + state, Trigger fired + reference), IndicatorsPanel (EMA13, EMA26, MACD Histogram, Bull Power, Bear Power). Decide and record as a decisions entry how (or whether) to add equivalent help to StockCharts' two charts (PriceChart's signal/EMA overlay, OscillatorChart's three panes) -- a chart doesn't have one obvious 'metric corner' the way a stat card does, so this may need a per-chart or per-legend-item treatment rather than the same per-value pattern, or may be reasonably deferred if the effort/value tradeoff doesn't justify it in this pass.

Build this as one reusable common/ component (e.g. a small question-mark IconButton that opens a Popover/Dialog with the explanation) plus a shared content registry (metric key -> {definition, elderContext, valueInterpreter(value) -> string}) rather than hand-writing a one-off tooltip at each call site -- this is exactly the kind of thing that should exist once and be reused, per the add-frontend-feature skill's common/-vs-feature-specific placement decision.

checklist.step: Design the shared help component (icon placement, trigger -- Popover vs Dialog vs MUI Tooltip with rich content -- and how the three-part explanation is laid out) and the content-registry shape (static definition + Elder-methodology context + an optional current-value interpreter function); record as a decisions entry with rationale.
Build the common/ component (e.g. common/MetricHelp) with its own test and Storybook story, following existing common/ component conventions.

Write the content-registry entries for every metric listed in the description, each grounded in a specific docs/Analyse.md section -- cite the section in the entry itself (e.g. a code comment) so drift from the doc is easy to catch later.

Wire the help icon into SignalSummary, ScreensPanel, and IndicatorsPanel for every metric they display, including a current-value interpretation wherever one can be meaningfully computed (not just a static definition).
Decide and implement (or explicitly defer with rationale) the equivalent treatment for StockCharts' two charts; record as a decisions entry.

Tests for the shared component and for at least a representative sample of wired-in call sites (not necessarily every single one, given the count) confirming the right explanation opens for the right metric.
Confirm 90% coverage gate still holds, Storybook build succeeds, and run make e2e to confirm nothing broke on the stock detail page.

decisions.decision: Built one new common/ component, `common/MetricHelp`, that renders only a small question-mark trigger (reusing `common/InfoBalloon`, from the merged frontend-signal-why-explanation PR #125, for the actual open/close/anchor Popover mechanism rather than a second balloon/popover implementation) with a fixed three-part content layout: a `definition` paragraph, an `elderContext` paragraph (methodology basis, citing a docs/Analyse.md section), and an optional bold `valueInterpretation` paragraph shown only when supplied. `MetricHelp` itself takes only plain strings and is domain-agnostic -- no Elder-specific typing -- so it stays reusable for any metric on any future page.
decisions.rationale: InfoBalloon already solves 'click a trigger, get an anchored explanation popover' generically (it was built with exactly this generalization in mind per its own doc comment); building a second Popover/Dialog mechanism for this task would duplicate that solved problem and violate the add-frontend-feature skill's near-duplicate-consolidation rule. A Popover (not a Dialog/modal) for the same reason InfoBalloon itself chose one: every call site's content here is a short, bounded explanation, not a form or long document needing the whole viewport. Rejected a design where MetricHelp itself contains Elder/Analyse.md-specific fields (e.g. typed `screen`/`component` enums) -- that would misplace domain knowledge into common/, failing Frontend.md §3's placement test; the actual Triple Screen/confidence content lives in the feature-level `metricHelpContent.ts` registry instead, keeping MetricHelp itself a thin, presentation-only building block.

decisions.decision: The content registry (`features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts`) is a plain object of named, individually-typed entries (`signalHelp`, `confidenceHelp`, `confidenceComponentHelp` keyed by the API's `confidence_breakdown[].component` string, `tideHelp`/`impulseHelp`/`waveHelp`/`triggerHelp`, `ema13Help`/`ema26Help`/`macdHistogramHelp`/`bullPowerHelp`/`bearPowerHelp`) rather than a single `Record<MetricKey, MetricHelpContent>` with one uniform `interpretValue(value: unknown) => string` signature.
decisions.rationale: The metrics covered are genuinely heterogeneous in what a meaningful current-value interpretation needs as input -- a signal string, a (confidence, band) pair, a (score, weight) pair, a (trend, slope) pair, a (stochasticK, forceIndex, state) triple, or a plain nullable number (sometimes compared against a sibling value, e.g. EMA13 vs EMA26). Forcing every entry through one `(value: unknown) => string` signature would have meant unsafe casts at every call site instead of the compiler catching a wrong-shaped call; named exports with their own concrete parameter types keep every call site fully type-checked. This still satisfies the checklist's 'metric key -> {definition, elderContext, valueInterpreter}' shape at the level of each individual entry -- the only change is that the outer collection isn't itself forced into one uniform TypeScript type.

decisions.decision: Help-icon placement varies per call site rather than one literal CSS absolute-top-right-corner overlay everywhere: ScreensPanel's four `ScreenSection` cards get a new `help` slot rendered inline in the existing title row (`justifyContent: 'space-between'`); IndicatorsPanel's five `StatCard`s use a new optional `corner` prop added to `common/StatCard` (rendered via `position: absolute; top: 4; right: 4` inside the card, only when supplied -- a small, backward-compatible extension, since it's `undefined` and renders nothing for every other existing StatCard caller on Dashboard/Portfolio); SignalSummary's Signal badge and Confidence gauge each get a trailing inline icon in their own row (not an overlay); each confidence_breakdown table row gets its own inline icon next to the component name in its cell.
decisions.rationale: A literal absolute-position overlay reads as 'in the corner' only against a large-enough host element (a Card); several of this task's targets are visually compact (a Chip-based SignalBadge, a LinearProgress-based ConfidenceGauge, a DataTable cell) where an overlapping absolute icon would read as 'on top of' rather than 'in the corner', and no test in this suite (or elsewhere in the codebase) asserts exact pixel placement, so there is no regression risk either way. Adding the `corner` slot directly to `common/StatCard` (rather than wrapping every StatCard call site in an ad hoc `position: relative` Box at each of the five IndicatorsPanel usages) centralizes the actual corner-overlay CSS in one place, the same way `PageHeader`'s existing `action` prop already establishes the pattern of a common/ component taking an arbitrary trailing `ReactNode` without needing to know what it is.

decisions.decision: Deferred adding MetricHelp-style help icons to StockCharts' two charts (PriceChart's candlestick + EMA13/EMA26 + signal-marker overlay, OscillatorChart's three panes) in this pass.
decisions.rationale: Both charts are built on Lightweight Charts' own canvas-rendered series/pane primitives (frontend-chart-signal-overlay, frontend-oscillator-chart), which have no DOM element per legend line to anchor a per-series MetricHelp trigger onto the way a Card/StatCard/table-cell does -- adding one would require either a custom DOM-overlay legend (a nontrivial new UI element neither chart currently has) or a single chart-level help icon that would necessarily be far less specific than every other help icon this task adds (one icon explaining three-to-five different series at once, rather than one icon per metric). Given the task description's own explicit 'may be reasonably deferred if the effort/value tradeoff doesn't justify it in this pass' allowance, and that IndicatorsPanel already gives every one of PriceChart's/OscillatorChart's plotted values (EMA13, EMA26, MACD Histogram, Stochastic %K via ScreensPanel's Wave section, Force Index via ScreensPanel's Wave section) full per-metric help coverage as plain stat values on the same page, this is deferred rather than built now. If a future pass wants per-series chart help, it should be tracked as its own follow-up task (e.g. a `frontend-stock-detail-metric-help-followups` entry, per CLAUDE.md's non-blocking-finding convention) rather than reopening this one.

decisions.decision: Fixed PR #127's blocking review finding by giving `triggerHelp.interpretValue` (metricHelpContent.ts) a third `tideTrend` parameter and branching its `not_applicable` message on it: `tideTrend === 'NEUTRAL'` now says the Trigger isn't evaluated because Screen 1 itself is Neutral (the common case, per `evaluate_trigger`'s own docstring -- NEUTRAL tide short-circuits before ever checking bar count), while any other tide value keeps the prior 'not enough daily price history yet' wording for the genuinely-rare <2-daily-bars case. `ScreensPanel.tsx`'s existing Trigger call site was updated to pass `tide.trend` (already in scope right next to `tideHelp.interpretValue`'s own use of it). Verified live against the fixture backend (uvicorn on FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture + vite dev, headless Playwright): AAPL (420 daily bars, Neutral tide) now renders 'Not applicable -- the Tide is Neutral...' instead of the previously-incorrect insufficient-history message. All four fixture tickers (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA/GOOGL) always carry 420 daily bars, so the fixture provider can never produce the genuinely-insufficient-history sub-case (`len(daily_ohlcv) < 2`) live -- that sub-case is covered by a direct unit test on `triggerHelp.interpretValue(false, 'not_applicable', 'BULLISH')` instead (metricHelpContent.test.ts), which is the only way to exercise it without a purpose-built short-history fixture.
decisions.rationale: A parameter addition (rather than e.g. duplicating triggerHelp into tide-aware/tide-unaware variants) keeps one function and one call site, matching every other interpretValue in this registry that already takes whatever siblings its message needs (waveHelp takes three, ema13Help/ema26Help each take the other EMA). Kept the two `not_applicable` causes as an if/else on `tideTrend` rather than having `evaluate_trigger` itself return a more granular `reference` value (e.g. distinguishing 'tide_neutral' from 'insufficient_history' in the API response) -- that would be a backend/API contract change (a new documented `reference` enum value in docs/architecture/API.md, an OpenAPI snapshot update, and a signal-engine test update) to fix what was purely a frontend-side misinterpretation of an already-correct, already-documented backend value; the frontend already had every input (`tide.trend`) it needed in scope at the one call site, so no such backend change was warranted for this fix.
decisions.verification: backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_trigger docstring/code confirms the two not_applicable causes; live-verified via headless Playwright against a fixture-mode backend + vite dev server that AAPL (Neutral tide) now shows the corrected message; frontend vitest suite (334/334 passing, 99.68% line / 99.42% branch coverage, both above the 90% gate); tsc --noEmit and eslint both clean; backend pytest unaffected (573/573 passing, no backend files touched).

decisions.decision: Also addressed, in this same pass, two of the three non-blocking follow-ups tracked at docs/tasks/frontend-stock-detail-metric-help-followups.json: (1) dropped common/MetricHelp's hardcoded, non-unique `data-testid="metric-help-icon"` (the existing per-instance `aria-label` of `${metricLabel} help`, already unique across every call site on the page, is the correct query target -- nothing in the codebase referenced the old testid); (2) tightened tideHelp.interpretValue's Neutral-case wording to distinguish a genuinely flat weekly MACD-H slope from a slope/EMA-relationship disagreement, the same family of fix as the blocking Trigger finding. Also added call-site-level tests to IndicatorsPanel.test.tsx, ScreensPanel.test.tsx, and SignalSummary.test.tsx (the third follow-up item) confirming the right MetricHelp opens with the right content when wired with real component props, including a direct regression test for this PR's Trigger/Neutral-tide fix.
decisions.rationale: All three were flagged as 'worth fixing now' or 'convenient' by the dispatching instruction and the followups task itself, are small, low-risk, in the exact files already being touched for the blocking fix, and (for the test-coverage gap) close a real gap the parent task's checklist had incorrectly claimed as done. Left the followups task's checklist items marked done with a note rather than deleting the task outright, since CLAUDE.md's tracked-follow-up convention treats it as the durable record of the finding regardless of when it's actually resolved.

comments.summary: Confirmed fix for the prior round's blocking finding: triggerHelp.interpretValue now takes a tideTrend parameter and branches its not_applicable message -- NEUTRAL tide gets 'Not applicable -- the Tide is Neutral...', any other tide value keeps the prior insufficient-daily-history wording for the genuinely rare <2-daily-bar case. Verified against backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_trigger (its two not_applicable causes match the two frontend branches exactly), independently reproduced live via a headless Playwright script against the fixture backend (AAPL, 420 daily bars, Neutral tide) confirming the balloon now reads 'Tide is Neutral' and not 'enough daily price history', and confirmed the <2-bar sub-case is covered by a direct unit test (metricHelpContent.test.ts) since no fixture ticker can produce it live. ScreensPanel.tsx's Trigger call site correctly passes tide.trend.

Confirmed the three round-1 non-blocking follow-ups are genuinely resolved in this pass: (1) MetricHelp's non-unique data-testid removed (aria-label is the query target); (2) new call-site tests in IndicatorsPanel.test.tsx/ScreensPanel.test.tsx/SignalSummary.test.tsx click a specific metric's help icon and assert that metric's specific rendered text appears (and a sibling metric's text does not) -- these are genuine content assertions, not mount-only checks; (3) tideHelp.interpretValue's Neutral-case wording now distinguishes a genuinely flat weekly MACD-H slope from a slope/EMA disagreement, matching evaluate_tide's own two paths for a computed (non-history-starved) NEUTRAL.

Non-blocking (new, found this round): tideHelp.interpretValue's new 'genuinely flat' branch is itself inaccurate for evaluate_tide's <2-weekly-bar short-circuit (triple_screen.py lines 154-155), which returns slope='flat' without ever computing a slope at all -- the same class of two-distinct-causes conflation this PR just fixed for triggerHelp, left unaddressed in tideHelp's own fix in the same pass. Narrower/rarer than the original Trigger bug (needs <2 weekly bars, which nothing in the current fixture set can produce) so not blocking, consistent with how the analogous <2-daily-bar Trigger sub-case was itself accepted via unit-test-only coverage last round. Tracked as a follow-up.

Non-blocking (new, found this round, pre-existing and outside this PR's diff): signalExplanation.ts's HOLD-explanation headline for a Neutral tide (the 'Why HOLD?' balloon, from the already-merged frontend-signal-why-explanation PR #125) unconditionally states 'the weekly MACD-Histogram slope and the 13/26-week EMA relationship disagree' even when the real cause is a genuinely flat slope -- the identical inaccuracy this PR's tideHelp fix just corrected, left uncorrected in a second, adjacent call site on the same page. Not part of this diff (signalExplanation.ts isn't touched), so not blocking this PR, but tracked as a follow-up since it now visibly contradicts the freshly-corrected tideHelp balloon right next to it for a flat-slope Neutral ticker.

review.notes: Retry round 2 of 3. Re-ran everything independently rather than trusting the report: backend pytest 99.86% (573 passed), frontend vitest 99.69%/99.42% (all files, 4 test files covering the touched code re-run individually and pass: 53/53), both well above the 90% gate, no regressions from round 1's numbers. ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean. make e2e: 13/13 passed (dashboard, navigation, portfolio, stock-analysis specs). Independently reproduced the round-1 blocking case live via a headless Playwright script against a freshly-started fixture-mode backend + vite dev server (not reusing the report's own claim): AAPL's Trigger help now shows 'Tide is Neutral' with no trace of the old insufficient-history text, and no console errors or failed network requests during the walkthrough. Read metricHelpContent.ts and ScreensPanel.tsx directly (not the report) and cross-checked both against backend/app/signals/triple_screen.py's evaluate_trigger/evaluate_tide docstrings and code -- the fix's branch logic matches the backend's actual two-cause split exactly. code-review skill (medium effort) run against the incremental diff surfaced two additional message-accuracy findings (both non-blocking, detailed above, filed as follow-ups) but no correctness bugs, regressions, or reuse/efficiency issues in the changed code itself. No API/schema changes in this diff, so no openapi.json check applies. No new frontend components added this round (only edits to existing MetricHelp/metricHelpContent/ScreensPanel/test files), so no new common/-vs-feature placement question beyond what round 1 already cleared. Non-blocking findings (2 new, on top of round 1's 3 already-resolved ones) added to docs/tasks/frontend-stock-detail-metric-help-followups.json.
